items.subject: eng

skill.th: การรับปากช่วยเหลือ

topic.th: บทสนทนา: การตอบโต้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the most appropriate response to complete the conversation.
A: Could you keep an eye on my bag while I grab a coffee?
B: ______ Take your time.

explanation.en: 'Take your time' shows B agrees, so 'Sure, no problem' fits. 'I'd rather not say' refuses to give information, 'Keep the change' is said when paying, and 'It's not my cup of tea' means B does not like something.
explanation.th: Take your time แสดงว่า B ยินดีช่วย จึงตอบ Sure, no problem ส่วน I'd rather not say คือไม่อยากบอก Keep the change ใช้ตอนจ่ายเงิน และ It's not my cup of tea แปลว่าไม่ชอบสิ่งนั้น

choices: It's not my cup of tea.

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การรับคำขอโทษ

topic.th: บทสนทนา: การตอบโต้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the most appropriate response to complete the conversation.
A: I'm sorry I snapped at you earlier. I'd had a terrible morning.
B: ______ We all have days like that.

explanation.en: 'We all have days like that' is forgiving, so B accepts the apology: 'Don't worry about it.' 'You should be' is cold, 'Same to you' returns a wish, and 'That's very kind of you' thanks someone for help.
explanation.th: We all have days like that เป็นการให้อภัย B จึงตอบ Don't worry about it ส่วน You should be ฟังดูเย็นชา Same to you ใช้ตอบคำอวยพร และ That's very kind of you ใช้ขอบคุณเมื่อได้รับความช่วยเหลือ

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Agreeing on a course of action
skill.th: การเห็นพ้องเรื่องสิ่งที่ควรทำ

topic.th: บทสนทนา: การตอบโต้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the most appropriate response to complete the conversation.
A: Do you think we should tell Krit that his essay is due tomorrow, not next week?
B: ______ He'd want to know, even if it ruins his evening.

explanation.en: B's reason — 'He'd want to know' — supports telling him, so 'I think we'd better' fits. The other replies all argue against telling Krit and contradict B's next sentence.
explanation.th: เหตุผลของ B คือ He'd want to know ซึ่งสนับสนุนให้บอก จึงตอบ I think we'd better ส่วนคำตอบอื่นล้วนไม่อยากบอก ขัดกับประโยคต่อมาของ B

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Offering to deal with a problem
skill.th: การอาสาจัดการปัญหา

topic.th: บทสนทนา: การตอบโต้ในชีวิตประจำวัน

items.stem:
Choose the most appropriate response to complete the conversation.
A: The new manager wants everyone to stay late on Friday.
B: Friday? But that's the night of the concert!
A: ______ I'll see if I can swap shifts with someone.

explanation.en: A then promises to try to swap shifts, so A is offering to handle the problem: 'Leave it with me.' 'Suit yourself' sounds indifferent, 'Over my dead body' is a strong refusal, and 'That's beside the point' dismisses B's worry.
explanation.th: A บอกต่อว่าจะลองขอแลกกะ แปลว่า A อาสาจัดการให้ จึงพูดว่า Leave it with me ส่วน Suit yourself ฟังดูไม่ใส่ใจ Over my dead body เป็นการปฏิเสธรุนแรง และ That's beside the point เป็นการปัดความกังวลของ B

items.subject: eng

skill.th: การอธิบายความลังเลที่ซ่อนอยู่

topic.th: บทสนทนา: ความหมายแฝง

items.stem:
Choose the most appropriate response to complete the conversation.
A: I hear you've been offered a place at the boarding school. Congratulations!
B: Thanks. It's a great opportunity, I suppose.
A: You don't sound very sure.
B: ______

explanation.en: 'I suppose' and A's comment show B has doubts, so B explains the reason for the hesitation: leaving friends behind. The other replies express certainty and do not explain why B sounds unsure.
explanation.th: คำว่า I suppose และความเห็นของ A แสดงว่า B ยังลังเล B จึงอธิบายเหตุผลว่าต้องจากเพื่อน ๆ ส่วนคำตอบอื่นแสดงความมั่นใจ ไม่ได้อธิบายว่าทำไม B ฟังดูไม่แน่ใจ

choices: Of course — it's the best school in the country.
Yes, I've never been more certain of anything.
Well, it means leaving all my friends behind.
That's because I've already accepted it.

items.subject: eng

skill.en: for / since with a period of time
skill.th: for / since กับช่วงเวลา

topic.th: กาล (tense)

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: My sister [[has been]] [[working]] at the hospital [[since]] five years and [[still]] enjoys it.

explanation.en: 'Five years' is a period of time, so it takes 'for'. 'Since' is used with a starting point, such as 'since 2021'.
explanation.th: five years เป็นช่วงระยะเวลา ต้องใช้ for ส่วน since ใช้กับจุดเริ่มต้น เช่น since 2021

items.subject: eng

skill.th: collocation: make a mistake

topic.th: คำปรากฏร่วม (collocation)

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: [[Doing]] a mistake in front of the whole class [[was]] embarrassing, but the teacher [[handled]] the situation [[kindly]].

explanation.en: We 'make' a mistake, not 'do' one: 'Making a mistake in front of the whole class…'.
explanation.th: ใช้ make a mistake ไม่ใช่ do a mistake จึงต้องเป็น Making a mistake in front of the whole class

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำที่มักสับสน: affect / effect

topic.th: รูปคำ (word form)

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: The scientists [[were]] [[unable]] to explain [[why]] the samples had been so badly [[effected]] by the heat.

explanation.en: The verb meaning 'to have an influence on' is 'affect': 'had been badly affected'. 'Effect' as a verb means 'to bring about'.
explanation.th: กริยาที่แปลว่าส่งผลกระทบคือ affect จึงเป็น had been badly affected ส่วน effect เมื่อเป็นกริยาแปลว่าทำให้เกิดขึ้น

items.subject: eng

skill.th: บุพบทที่ตามมา: married to

topic.th: คำบุพบท

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: My aunt, [[who]] [[is married with]] a surgeon, [[rarely]] sees her husband [[before]] midnight.

explanation.en: In English we are 'married to' someone, not 'married with' them.
explanation.th: ภาษาอังกฤษใช้ married to someone ไม่ใช่ married with

items.subject: eng

skill.th: despite ไม่ต้องมี of

topic.th: คำเชื่อม

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: [[Despite of]] the heavy rain, thousands of fans [[queued]] outside the stadium [[for]] hours [[to buy]] tickets.

explanation.en: 'Despite' is followed directly by a noun: 'Despite the heavy rain'. 'Of' belongs only in 'in spite of'.
explanation.th: Despite ตามด้วยคำนามได้ทันที เป็น Despite the heavy rain ส่วน of ใช้เฉพาะใน in spite of

items.subject: eng

skill.en: No repeated object in a relative clause
skill.th: ไม่ใส่กรรมซ้ำในอนุประโยค relative

topic.th: อนุประโยค relative

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: The government is [[considering]] [[introducing]] a tax on sugary drinks, a measure [[that]] health experts have long [[argued for it]].

explanation.en: 'That' already stands for 'a measure' as the object of 'argued for', so 'it' repeats the object. It should be 'a measure that health experts have long argued for'.
explanation.th: that แทน a measure ซึ่งเป็นกรรมของ argued for อยู่แล้ว การใส่ it จึงเป็นกรรมซ้ำ ต้องเป็น a measure that health experts have long argued for

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Not only … but also with inversion
skill.th: Not only … but also กับการสลับที่

topic.th: การสลับที่ประธานกับกริยา (inversion)

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: Not only [[did]] the storm [[damage]] the harvest, [[but also it destroyed]] several homes [[along]] the coast.

explanation.en: After an inverted 'Not only' clause, the second clause keeps normal order with 'also' after the subject: 'but it also destroyed' (or 'but also destroyed').
explanation.th: เมื่อประโยคแรกขึ้นต้นด้วย Not only แบบสลับที่แล้ว ประโยคหลังเรียงตามปกติ โดย also อยู่หลังประธาน เป็น but it also destroyed (หรือ but also destroyed)

items.subject: eng

skill.th: adjective + บุพบท: responsible for

topic.th: คำบุพบท

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: Each prefect is [[held]] [[responsible of]] the behaviour of younger students [[during]] assemblies and [[on]] school trips.

explanation.en: The adjective 'responsible' takes 'for': 'held responsible for the behaviour'.
explanation.th: adjective responsible ใช้คู่กับ for จึงต้องเป็น held responsible for the behaviour

items.subject: eng

skill.th: relative pronoun: ใช้ that/which ไม่ใช่ what

topic.th: อนุประโยค relative

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: The data [[collected]] over the past decade [[clearly]] [[show]] a pattern [[what]] few had expected.

explanation.en: 'What' means 'the thing that' and cannot follow a noun. After 'a pattern' we need 'that' or 'which'. ('The data show' is acceptable, as 'data' is often plural.)
explanation.th: what แปลว่า 'สิ่งที่' และใช้ตามหลังคำนามไม่ได้ หลัง a pattern ต้องใช้ that หรือ which (The data show ถูกต้อง เพราะ data มักใช้เป็นพหูพจน์)

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Past participle in a comparison phrase
skill.th: past participle ในวลีเปรียบเทียบ

topic.th: participle clause

items.stem: Choose the underlined part that is incorrect: [[Comparing]] with last year's figures, this year's exports [[have]] [[grown]] [[considerably]].

explanation.en: Exports do not compare anything; they are compared. The passive form is needed: 'Compared with last year's figures…'.
explanation.th: ยอดส่งออกไม่ได้เป็นผู้เปรียบเทียบ แต่ถูกนำมาเปรียบเทียบ จึงต้องใช้รูป passive คือ Compared with last year's figures

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Word form: adverb before a participle
skill.th: รูปคำ: adverb ขยาย participle

topic.th: เติมคำในบทความข่าว/สารคดี

items.passage: Maya Bay, the beach made famous by a Hollywood film, was closed to visitors in 2018 after years of mass tourism had left its coral reefs (1) ______ damaged. At its peak, the bay received several thousand visitors a day, and boats regularly dropped anchor directly on the reef. Scientists warned that, (2) ______ urgent action was taken, the damage could become permanent. The closure, initially intended to last a few months, was (3) ______ extended several times. During that period, marine biologists planted thousands of young corals, and blacktip reef sharks, which had all but (4) ______ from the area, began to return. When the bay finally reopened, strict rules had been (5) ______ place: swimming was banned, visitor numbers were capped and boats had to dock on the far side of the island.
items.stem: Which option best fills gap (1)?

explanation.en: The past participle 'damaged' is modified by an adverb: 'severely damaged'. 'Severe' is an adjective, 'severity' a noun, and 'sever' a verb meaning 'cut off'.
explanation.th: past participle damaged ต้องขยายด้วย adverb จึงเป็น severely damaged ส่วน severe เป็น adjective, severity เป็นคำนาม และ sever เป็นกริยาแปลว่าตัดขาด

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำเชื่อมเงื่อนไข: unless

topic.th: เติมคำในบทความข่าว/สารคดี

items.passage: Maya Bay, the beach made famous by a Hollywood film, was closed to visitors in 2018 after years of mass tourism had left its coral reefs (1) ______ damaged. At its peak, the bay received several thousand visitors a day, and boats regularly dropped anchor directly on the reef. Scientists warned that, (2) ______ urgent action was taken, the damage could become permanent. The closure, initially intended to last a few months, was (3) ______ extended several times. During that period, marine biologists planted thousands of young corals, and blacktip reef sharks, which had all but (4) ______ from the area, began to return. When the bay finally reopened, strict rules had been (5) ______ place: swimming was banned, visitor numbers were capped and boats had to dock on the far side of the island.
items.stem: Which option best fills gap (2)?

explanation.en: The damage would become permanent if action was NOT taken, so 'unless' is needed. 'If', 'provided' and 'as long as' would mean that taking action causes permanent damage.
explanation.th: ความเสียหายจะถาวรถ้า 'ไม่' ลงมือแก้ไข จึงใช้ unless ส่วน if, provided และ as long as จะให้ความหมายว่าการลงมือแก้ไขทำให้เสียหายถาวร ซึ่งไม่สมเหตุสมผล

items.subject: eng

skill.th: adverb บอกเวลา: subsequently

topic.th: เติมคำในบทความข่าว/สารคดี

items.passage: Maya Bay, the beach made famous by a Hollywood film, was closed to visitors in 2018 after years of mass tourism had left its coral reefs (1) ______ damaged. At its peak, the bay received several thousand visitors a day, and boats regularly dropped anchor directly on the reef. Scientists warned that, (2) ______ urgent action was taken, the damage could become permanent. The closure, initially intended to last a few months, was (3) ______ extended several times. During that period, marine biologists planted thousands of young corals, and blacktip reef sharks, which had all but (4) ______ from the area, began to return. When the bay finally reopened, strict rules had been (5) ______ place: swimming was banned, visitor numbers were capped and boats had to dock on the far side of the island.
items.stem: Which option best fills gap (3)?

explanation.en: The closure was planned for a few months and then extended later, so 'subsequently' (afterwards) fits. 'Previously', 'formerly' and 'beforehand' all refer to an earlier time.
explanation.th: เดิมตั้งใจปิดไม่กี่เดือนแล้วจึงขยายเวลาภายหลัง จึงใช้ subsequently (ต่อมา) ส่วน previously, formerly และ beforehand หมายถึงช่วงก่อนหน้า

items.subject: eng

skill.th: past perfect กับ all but

topic.th: เติมคำในบทความข่าว/สารคดี

items.passage: Maya Bay, the beach made famous by a Hollywood film, was closed to visitors in 2018 after years of mass tourism had left its coral reefs (1) ______ damaged. At its peak, the bay received several thousand visitors a day, and boats regularly dropped anchor directly on the reef. items.subject: eng

skill.th: collocation: put in place

topic.th: เติมคำในบทความข่าว/สารคดี

items.passage: Maya Bay, the beach made famous by a Hollywood film, was closed to visitors in 2018 after years of mass tourism had left its coral reefs (1) ______ damaged. At its peak, the bay received several thousand visitors a day, and boats regularly dropped anchor directly on the reef. Scientists warned that, (2) ______ urgent action was taken, the damage could become permanent. The closure, initially intended to last a few months, was (3) ______ extended several times. During that period, marine biologists planted thousands of young corals, and blacktip reef sharks, which had all but (4) ______ from the area, began to return. When the bay finally reopened, strict rules had been (5) ______ place: swimming was banned, visitor numbers were capped and boats had to dock on the far side of the island.
items.stem: Which option best fills gap (5)?

explanation.en: Rules or systems are 'put in place' (introduced and made active). 'Taken in', 'made in' and 'held in' do not form this expression.
explanation.th: กฎหรือระบบใช้สำนวน put in place (นำมาใช้) ส่วน taken in, made in และ held in ไม่ได้เป็นสำนวนนี้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: สำนวน: pluck up the courage

topic.th: เติมคำในเรื่องสั้น

items.passage: The letter had been sitting on the kitchen table for three days before Arthit (6) ______ up the courage to open it. He already knew what it would say — or thought he did. His older brother had been accepted by the same university without difficulty, and his parents (7) ______ that he would follow. As he unfolded the page, his hands were trembling so much that he had to read the first line twice. "We regret to inform you…" He sat down slowly. Strangely, the feeling that (8) ______ over him was not disappointment but something closer to relief. For years he had been preparing for a future that (9) ______ never really been his own. Now, for the first time, he would have to decide what he actually wanted — a prospect that was as (10) ______ as it was frightening.
items.stem: Which option best fills gap (6)?

explanation.en: The idiom is 'pluck up the courage' (find enough bravery to do something). 'Pull up', 'pick up' and 'bring up' do not combine with 'the courage' in this way.
explanation.th: สำนวนคือ pluck up the courage (รวบรวมความกล้า) ส่วน pull up, pick up และ bring up ไม่ใช้กับ the courage ในความหมายนี้

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Expression: take it for granted that
skill.th: สำนวน: take it for granted that

topic.th: เติมคำในเรื่องสั้น

items.passage: The letter had been sitting on the kitchen table for three days before Arthit (6) ______ up the courage to open it. He already knew what it would say — or thought he did. His older brother had been accepted by the same university without difficulty, and his parents (7) ______ that he would follow. As he unfolded the page, his hands were trembling so much that he had to read the first line twice. "We regret to inform you…" He sat down slowly. Strangely, the feeling that (8) ______ over him was not disappointment but something closer to relief. For years he had been preparing for a future that (9) ______ never really been his own. Now, for the first time, he would have to decide what he actually wanted — a prospect that was as (10) ______ as it was frightening.
items.stem: Which option best fills gap (7)?

explanation.en: Before a 'that' clause, the pattern needs the dummy object 'it': 'take it for granted that…'. Without 'it' the structure is incomplete, and the passive would make the parents the thing assumed.
explanation.th: เมื่อตามด้วย that clause ต้องมี it เป็นกรรมแทน: take it for granted that… ถ้าไม่มี it โครงสร้างไม่สมบูรณ์ และรูป passive จะกลายเป็นว่าพ่อแม่ถูกคาดเอาเอง

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Past simple in a relative clause
skill.th: past simple ในอนุประโยค relative

topic.th: เติมคำในเรื่องสั้น

items.passage: The letter had been sitting on the kitchen table for three days before Arthit (6) ______ up the courage to open it. He already knew what it would say — or thought he did. His older brother had been accepted by the same university without difficulty, and his parents (7) ______ that he would follow. As he unfolded the page, his hands were trembling so much that he had to read the first line twice. "We regret to inform you…" He sat down slowly. Strangely, the feeling that (8) ______ over him was not disappointment but something closer to relief. For years he had been preparing for a future that (9) ______ never really been his own. Now, for the first time, he would have to decide what he actually wanted — a prospect that was as (10) ______ as it was frightening.
items.stem: Which option best fills gap (8)?

explanation.en: The relative clause needs a finite past verb: 'the feeling that washed over him'. 'Washing' is not finite, 'was washed' is wrongly passive, and 'wash' is the wrong tense.
explanation.th: อนุประโยค relative ต้องมีกริยาแท้ในอดีต: the feeling that washed over him ส่วน washing ไม่ใช่กริยาแท้ was washed เป็น passive ที่ผิดความหมาย และ wash ผิด tense

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Past perfect for an earlier situation
skill.th: past perfect สำหรับสภาพการณ์ที่ต่อเนื่องมาก่อน

topic.th: เติมคำในเรื่องสั้น

items.passage: The letter had been sitting on the kitchen table for three days before Arthit (6) ______ up the courage to open it. He already knew what it would say — or thought he did. His older brother had been accepted by the same university without difficulty, and his parents (7) ______ that he would follow. As he unfolded the page, his hands were trembling so much that he had to read the first line twice. "We regret to inform you…" He sat down slowly. Strangely, the feeling that (8) ______ over him was not disappointment but something closer to relief. For years he had been preparing for a future that (9) ______ never really been his own. Now, for the first time, he would have to decide what he actually wanted — a prospect that was as (10) ______ as it was frightening.
items.stem: Which option best fills gap (9)?

explanation.en: 'Been' needs a perfect auxiliary, and the story is in the past, so 'had never really been his own'. 'Has' is the wrong tense, and 'was been' and 'would been' are ungrammatical.

items.passage:
BANGKOK — Motor vehicles will be banned from a two-kilometre stretch of the city's historic Rattanakosin district every Sunday from next month, under a six-month trial announced by city officials on Tuesday.

The scheme will close several roads near the Grand Palace to private cars, taxis and motorcycles between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m., turning them over to pedestrians, cyclists and street performers. Residents will be issued permits allowing them to drive to and from their homes at walking pace, and a free electric shuttle bus will link the zone to the nearest metro stations.

Officials say the trial is intended to reduce air pollution and make the area more pleasant for the millions of tourists who visit each year. "Our old town was built for people, not engines," a deputy governor told reporters. "For one day a week, we want to give it back to them."

The announcement drew a mixed response. Shop owners on one of the affected roads, where many businesses rely on deliveries, said they had not been consulted. "Of course we want clean air," said one restaurant owner. "But if suppliers cannot reach us on our busiest day, the clean air will be very quiet."

Taxi drivers' associations have also raised objections, arguing that the closures will simply push traffic onto surrounding roads. Transport researchers say that risk is real but often overstated. Studies of similar schemes in other Asian cities have found that congestion in neighbouring streets typically rises for the first few weeks before settling below its original level, as drivers change their routes or leave their cars at home.

City officials have promised to review the trial after three months and say they are open to adjusting delivery hours. Whether the scheme becomes permanent, they added, will depend largely on what residents and businesses make of it.

explanation.en: The first two paragraphs say cars, taxis and motorcycles will be banned from a two-kilometre stretch between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m., with exceptions for residents. It is not the whole city, and it is the shuttle bus, not the metro, that is free.

items.passage:
At twelve, Nok was the best English speaker in her family, which meant that whenever her father had to deal with the outside world, Nok went with him. She translated letters from the bank, phone calls from the landlord and, once, a long argument with a man who had reversed into their car.

She was proud of the job, mostly. It made her feel grown-up, and adults sometimes looked at her with a kind of surprised respect. But there were moments when she wished she could simply be a child who did not understand.

The worst of these came on a grey Tuesday in the doctor's office. The doctor spoke quickly, glancing at her screen rather than at Nok's father. Nok caught words she knew — "results", "further tests" — and others she did not. Then the doctor said, "I'm afraid it's not good news," and looked, finally, at Nok, waiting.

Her father was watching her face. Nok understood, in that instant, that whatever she said next would become true for him in a way it was not yet true for her.

"She says they need to do more tests," Nok said in Thai. "She says not to worry yet."

It was not exactly a lie. The doctor had said something about tests. Her father nodded, and some of the tightness left his shoulders.

On the bus home he bought her a mango smoothie, the expensive kind, and talked about football. Nok held the cup with both hands and did not drink it. She was thinking about the word "yet", and about how much weight one small word could carry, and about the second appointment, next Thursday, when she would have to choose again.

explanation.en: The first sentence says she 'was the best English speaker in her family', which is why she goes with him.

Daniel Reyes wakes at four-thirty every morning, and he would very much like you to know it. In Ten Thousand Mornings, his third book on what he calls "deliberate living", Reyes argues that the hours before dawn are the key to a successful life, and that almost anyone who claims to be too busy to achieve their goals is simply sleeping through the solution.

There is something here worth taking seriously. Reyes is good on the value of routine, and his chapter on protecting time for difficult work — switching off notifications, saying no to unnecessary meetings — contains advice that many readers will find useful. His prose is clear and occasionally funny, particularly when he describes his own early failures, such as the morning he fell asleep in the middle of a meditation session and woke with his face in a bowl of oatmeal.

The problems begin when Reyes moves from describing what works for him to prescribing what should work for everyone. His readers, it seems, are assumed to have flexible jobs, no young children and no need to work a night shift. A single mother who writes to say that she cannot possibly rise at four-thirty is gently told that she has "not yet found her why". One suspects she has found it; it is asleep in the next room.

Reyes cites a great deal of research, but rather selectively. Studies that support early rising are described in detail, while the considerable evidence that people's natural sleep patterns differ — and that forcing an early schedule on a "night owl" can harm health — appears only in a brief footnote.

Readers who already enjoy early mornings will find much here to confirm what they believe. Those who do not may wish to read it in the afternoon, which is, after all, when most of us are properly awake.

Most of us think of memory as a kind of recording: an event happens, the brain stores it, and when we remember, we press "play". It is a comforting idea. It is also, according to several decades of psychological research, almost entirely wrong.

Memories, it turns out, are not retrieved so much as rebuilt. Each time we recall an event, the brain reassembles it from scattered fragments — a sound, a feeling, a fact — and fills the gaps with whatever seems most plausible. The result usually feels vivid and certain. That feeling, unfortunately, is a poor guide to accuracy.

In a well-known series of studies, participants watched a film of a car accident and were then asked how fast the cars were going when they "smashed into" or "hit" each other. Those who heard the word "smashed" gave higher estimates, and a week later they were more likely to report having seen broken glass, although there had been none. A single verb had quietly rewritten what they remembered.

The implications reach well beyond the laboratory. Eyewitness testimony, long regarded as among the most persuasive forms of evidence in a courtroom, is now known to be a leading factor in wrongful convictions. Witnesses are rarely lying; they are simply reporting, with complete sincerity, a memory that has been shaped by leading questions, by news reports or by their own expectations.

Yet it would be a mistake to see this flexibility as merely a flaw. A memory system that rebuilds rather than replays allows us to combine past experiences in new ways — to imagine the future, to draw general lessons from particular events, to tell stories. The price of that creativity is a certain unreliability. It is a price, perhaps, that we should simply learn to keep in mind.

In a well-known series of studies, participants watched a film of a car accident and were then asked how fast the cars were going when they "smashed into" or "hit" each other. Those who heard the word "smashed" gave higher estimates, and a week later they were more likely to report having seen broken glass, although there had been none. A single verb had quietly rewritten what they remembered.

The implications reach well beyond the laboratory. Eyewitness testimony, long regarded as among the most persuasive forms of evidence in a courtroom, is now known to be a leading factor in wrongful convictions. Witnesses are rarely lying; they are simply reporting, with complete sincerity, a memory that has been shaped by leading questions, by news reports or by their own expectations.

Yet it would be a mistake to see this flexibility as merely a flaw. A memory system that rebuilds rather than replays allows us to combine past experiences in new ways — to imagine the future, to draw general lessons from particular events, to tell stories. The price of that creativity is a certain unreliability. It is a price, perhaps, that we should simply learn to keep in mind.
